title: Minaeans
capsule: The Minaeans (Ma'in) were a South Arabian kingdom occupying the Jawf valley of what is now northern Yemen, attested from at least the fourth century BCE and flourishing as a major incense-trade intermediary between Arabia Felix and the Mediterranean world. Their commercial reach extended north along the Hejaz caravan routes to colonies at Dedan (al-Ula) in the Hejaz and even into the Nile Delta, documented by Minaean dedicatory inscriptions found across the Near East. The kingdom declined in the first century BCE under pressure from the expanding Sabaean kingdom to the south and was absorbed, with the Sabaeans dominating South Arabia by the late first century BCE.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The Minaean heartland in the Jawf valley is attested by abundant inscriptions; the outer extent of political (as opposed to commercial) authority is poorly defined and colonial outposts represent trade influence rather than territorial control.
